notes.summary: Public-primary-source audit of the explicitly permitted foundations. No continuous-coefficient Fredholm theorem or conclusion A–E is imported. Source transcripts and reproducible artifacts are saved; unrestricted P16 remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Records the permitted original normalization, concavity, support and L^q facts, and verifies the relevant bounded-product, Fourier-multiplier, smooth ABP and smooth stationary-probability premises at public primary sources. Gauduchon's Theorem 2 has no even-Betti restriction. Standard Sobolev and smooth elliptic foundations remain expressly admitted rather than recursively certified. No credentials, other workers, private reports or verifier histories were inspected. The unidentified historical product-adjoint attribution is not used.
notes.text:
This deliverable independently reconstructs the restricted assignment A–E as ordinary unverified mathematical drafts. It does not resolve the original every-continuous-density P16 question.

The original task expressly permits normalization-scalar uniqueness, concavity, monotonicity, B0(F+c)=B0(F)-c, nonempty weakly compact supporting sets, and support densities in every L^q with 1<q<n/(n-1). These are the original facts used below. A support always means a probability satisfying the defining inequality for ALL real continuous G.

The other admitted foundations used are: genuine canonical psh representatives and radial regularization; recursively defined bounded Bedford–Taylor products and decreasing continuity; the order-zero Fourier multiplier theorem; smooth Sobolev density and extension, W^(2,p) embedding into C^(1,alpha) for p greater than the real dimension, compact W^(2,p) inclusion into L^p, Holder duality and reflexive weak compactness; the smooth ABP bound; classical smooth elliptic regularity and Fredholm theory, smooth shifted-Laplacian invertibility, Neumann's lemma, method of continuity and compact-perturbation invariance of index; smooth Gauduchon stationary probabilities; smooth Stokes, sphere Green kernels, Fubini, elementary matrix algebra and modulus estimates, and H^2(S^3 times S^1,R)=0. No continuous-coefficient Fredholm theorem, rough adjoint theorem, nonsmooth Schauder estimate or unspecified rough generator is admitted.

Public primary sources actually inspected on 2026-10-08:

1. [Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf), Chapter I, printed pp.35–40, I.4.18, I.5.5 and I.5.8. The statements and proofs give decreasing radial regularization and the unique genuine locally integrable psh representative of a distribution with positive complex Hessian. The text distinguishes that representative from arbitrary a.e.-equal upper semicontinuous modifications. Only positive radially symmetric kernels are used here.

2. [Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), Acta Math.149 (1982),1–40, printed pp.4–7, Theorem2.1, Corollary2.2 and their proof. The recursively defined locally bounded psh products are symmetric and multilinear and converge for decreasing potentials. This grants the closed psh products only. The nonclosed-background application and uniform Hessian identification are proved in n3. Changes of the dd^c normalization rescale each Hessian factor and do not change these conclusions.

3. [Taylor, PDE III, Chapter13](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2018/04/chap13.pdf), Theorem5.1 and its Calderon–Zygmund proof context, printed pp.16–21, and the compactness proof at equation(6.9), p.24. The multiplier hypothesis is |D^alpha P(xi)|<=C_alpha<xi>^(-|alpha|), |alpha|<=m+1, in real dimension m. It grants constant-coefficient order-zero L^p multipliers. Lemma5.6 is a printed exercise, whose kernel-difference integral estimate follows from the mean-value theorem and integration of C|y||x-x0|^(-m-1) outside |x-x0|>=2t, for |y|<=t. It is not represented as a separately printed proof.

4. [Taylor, nonlinear elliptic chapter](https://mtaylor.web.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/16915/2020/08/nlellip.pdf), Section13, printed pp.143–145, Proposition13.1, Lemma13.2 and the complete contact-set proof. Its smooth ABP estimate uses a measurable uniformly positive principal matrix and no coefficient derivatives. Its separate mention of an Alexandrov Sobolev theorem without proof is not imported. The W^(2,p) passage and strong maximum principle required here are proved in n2.

5. [Gauduchon, Astérisque126 (1985),129–135](https://numdam.org/item/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf), printed pp.132–133, Theorem2 and both adjoint-kernel lemmas. They provide the positive smooth one-dimensional adjoint kernel, and hence the normalized stationary probability, for the smooth complex Laplacian. The even-Betti surface restriction belongs to Theorem1 and is absent from Theorem2. Sign and positive constant changes of the Laplacian do not affect stationarity. In complex dimension one, normalized area is stationary by Stokes.

This audit does not recursively certify every admitted standard Sobolev or smooth elliptic result. It verifies the particular primary-source premises above, without attributing A–E to those sources. No author proof of A–E, private note, other worker or verifier history was inspected. A public search did not identify the unspecified earlier product-adjoint argument mentioned in E; no historical claim from it is used.

Reproducibility: input.json preserves the supplied input. Public-source query/read results are saved in sources/web-1.json through web-4.json, sources/read-1.json through read-9.json, and sources/overlap-search.json. notes.summary: B reconstructed for every finite p>2n: L_sigma with continuous positive coefficients is Fredholm of index zero, has constants as kernel, and has a one-dimensional L^(p') range annihilator. Freezing, Sobolev maximum principles and the global continuity argument are proved.
notes.detailedSummary: Defines L_sigma using weak second derivatives and continuous inverse coefficients. Derives a constant-coefficient multiplier estimate, coefficient-freezing estimate, cutoff localization and finite-difference interpolation. Extends smooth ABP through W^(2,p) approximation and proves the strong maximum principle by an exponential tangent-annulus barrier and C^1 regularity. Establishes uniform shifted estimates and method-of-continuity invertibility, then Fredholmness by compact perturbation. The original L^q density bounds justify the duality step identifying normalized supporting probabilities.
notes.text:
Proof of B for every finite real p>2n. Put m=2n. Work with real Banach spaces and the fixed smooth dV; coordinate smooth-volume norms are equivalent.

For any continuous positive Hermitian sigma define
L_sigma h=tr_sigma(dd^c h), h in W^(2,p)(X).
The weak second derivatives of h are in L^p, and multiplication by the continuous matrix sigma^(-1) is bounded on L^p. This defines the operator without differentiating sigma. In holomorphic coordinates it has real expression a^(ij)(x)D_iD_j h, with a continuous symmetric positive real matrix, uniformly elliptic on relatively compact charts. There are no first- or zeroth-order terms. The positive factor from dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2 pi) is included in a. The scalar expression is coordinate invariant for smooth functions and therefore for Sobolev functions by smooth approximation.

1. Constant-coefficient estimate and coefficient freezing.

For a constant positive matrix a0 put Q(xi)=a0^(ij)xi_i xi_j. The symbols -xi_i xi_j/(1+Q(xi)) satisfy the admitted order-zero multiplier estimates. Applied to (1-a0^(ij)D_iD_j)v, they give, for v in C_c^infinity(R^m),
||D^2v||_p<=C0(||a0^(ij)D_iD_jv||_p+||v||_p). (1)
The denominator removes the origin singularity. The constants may be uniform over a compact uniformly elliptic matrix family: apply the estimate for a fixed matrix a* to a nearby a0, substitute a*D^2v=a0D^2v+(a*-a0)D^2v, and absorb the difference. A finite cover of the compact matrix family supplies one constant. No continuity of an unspecified multiplier norm is assumed.

On a chart ball choose a0=a(x0). Shrink the ball until C0 times the contraction-norm oscillation of a is less than 1/2. For v supported there, substitute a0D^2v=Lv+(a0-a)D^2v into (1) and absorb, obtaining
||D^2v||_p<=2C0(||Lv||_p+||v||_p). (2)
This is the coefficient-freezing estimate.

For a smooth cutoff chi,
L(chi h)=chi Lh+2a^(ij)(D_i chi)(D_j h)+(Lchi)h.
No coefficient is differentiated. A finite holomorphic chart cover and partition of unity give
||h||_(W^(2,p))<=C(||Lh||_p+||Dh||_p+||h||_p).
The first-derivative term is removed explicitly. For compactly supported Euclidean v,
D_i v(x)=(v(x+t e_i)-v(x))/t-(1/t)int_0^t(t-s)D_ii v(x+s e_i)ds.
Minkowski's inequality gives ||Dv||_p<=C(t||D^2v||_p+t^(-1)||v||_p). Apply this to partitioned functions and absorb the fixed cutoff terms involving t||Dh|| for small t. Thus, for every delta>0,
||Dh||_p<=delta||h||_(W^(2,p))+C_delta||h||_p.
Consequently
||h||_(W^(2,p))<=C(||Lh||_p+||h||_p). (3)
Initially proved for smooth h, this extends by admitted smooth Sobolev density and boundedness of L to every W^(2,p) h. A compact continuous uniformly elliptic coefficient family has a common modulus of continuity on the finite charts, so the freezing radii and constants may be uniform along that family. No Schauder estimate is used.

2. Maximum principles at actual W^(2,p) regularity.

Let D be a ball or smooth bounded annulus whose closure is inside a holomorphic chart. Extend v in W^(2,p)(D) across the boundary and approximate strongly by smooth v_j. Since p>m, embedding gives uniform C^1 convergence on the closure. Boundedness of a gives Lv_j to Lv in L^p and hence L^m on D. Positive-part truncation is Lipschitz in L^m. Passing the admitted smooth ABP bound to the limit therefore gives
sup_D v<=sup_boundaryD v+C||(-Lv)_+||_(L^m(D)). (4)
The boundary supremum is the continuous trace. In particular Lv>=0 a.e. implies the weak maximum principle.

For the strong principle, suppose v in W_loc^(2,p)(U), U connected, Lv>=0, and v attains its maximum M over U at an interior point. Set Z={v=M}. If Z is not all of U, it has a relative boundary. In a small chart about such a boundary choose y in U\Z sufficiently close to Z, put r=dist(y,Z), and ensure the closed ball stays in the chart. It touches Z at an outer point x and has v<M throughout its interior.

On r/2<|z-y|<r use
phi(z)=exp(-alpha|z-y|^2)-exp(-alpha r^2).
If lambda I<=a<=Lambda I, then
Lphi=exp(-alpha|z-y|^2)[4alpha^2 a^(ij)(z-y)_i(z-y)_j-2alpha tr a]>0
for alpha>2mLambda/(lambda r^2). The inner sphere has a positive minimum of M-v, so choose epsilon>0 with v-M+epsilon phi<=0 there. This inequality also holds on the outer sphere. Its L is nonnegative; (4) gives M-v>=epsilon phi on the annulus. Along the inward radius at x,
phi(x-t(x-y)/r)=2alpha r exp(-alpha r^2)t+o(t).
But v is C^1 and has an interior maximum at x, so Dv(x)=0 and M-v along this radius is o(t), a contradiction. Thus Z=U and v is constant. This proves the strong principle used here without importing a rough theorem.

On compact connected X, a W^(2,p) solution Lh=0 attains its maximum and is constant. For lambda0>0, a solution of (L-lambda0)h=0 cannot have a positive maximum: on a connected neighborhood where h>0, Lh=lambda0 h>=0, so the strong principle would make h constant there, contradicting Lh=lambda0 h>0. Applying this to -h excludes a negative minimum. Hence L-lambda0 is injective at exactly the required regularity.

3. Global Fredholm argument.

Choose a smooth positive Hermitian tau and join its trace operator to L_sigma by L_s=(1-s)L_tau+sL_sigma, 0<=s<=1. The family is continuous in operator norm W^(2,p) to L^p, uniformly elliptic and equicontinuous on each holomorphic chart. Estimate (3) is uniform and implies
||h||_(W^(2,p))<=C(||(L_s-lambda0)h||_p+||h||_p). (5)
Its lower norm can be removed uniformly. Otherwise there exist s_j to s and ||h_j||_(W^(2,p))=1 with (L_sj-lambda0)h_j to0 in L^p. A subsequence converges weakly in W^(2,p) and strongly in L^p to h. Operator-norm convergence gives (L_s-lambda0)h=0. Injectivity gives h=0, and (5) contradicts the unit norm. Therefore
||h||_(W^(2,p))<=C'||(L_s-lambda0)h||_p (6)
uniformly in s.

The initial smooth L_tau-lambda0 is an isomorphism by admitted smooth elliptic theory. More explicitly, smooth positive principal-symbol interpolation to a real Laplacian gives index zero; the maximum argument gives zero kernel. Neumann's lemma makes the isomorphism parameters open. They are closed: if s_j to s and the preceding operators are onto, solve (L_sj-lambda0)h_j=f for fixed f. Estimate (6) bounds the solutions; weak W^(2,p) and strong L^p compactness yield a solution at s. Injectivity and (6) provide its bounded inverse. Thus every parameter is an isomorphism. This proves the continuous-coefficient extension rather than asserting a smooth core for an unspecified operator.

Finally L_sigma=(L_sigma-lambda0)+lambda0 I, and I:W^(2,p) to L^p is compact. Compact-perturbation invariance gives Fredholm index zero. Its kernel is the constants, so its closed range has codimension one. Holder duality identifies its annihilator
N_p={rho in L^(p')(dV): int_X rho L_sigma h dV=0 for all h in W^(2,p)}, p'=p/(p-1),
as a one-dimensional space. This proves B.

4. Duality consequence for the original supports.

For p>2n, one has 1<p'<n/(n-1). Choose q strictly between p' and n/(n-1). An original supporting probability has L^q density by the supplied bound and thus has L^(p') density, since dV has finite mass. If it annihilates L_sigma on smooth tests, smooth Sobolev approximation and Holder's inequality extend annihilation to all W^(2,p) tests. Its density belongs to N_p. Two such probability densities are proportional because dim N_p=1; their integrals both equal1, forcing equality. Absolute continuity alone would not justify this argument.

Evidence and limitations: this is a mathematical proof conditional on n1's expressly admitted foundations. No coefficient is differentiated, rough formal adjoint formed, or generator core assumed. check_identities.py checks the duality window with p=2n+1 for the finite set n=2,...,20; that finite result is not the proof of the general inequality above. Output: artifacts/check-output.json. Authoritative artifact: artifacts/n2_fredholm.txt. Rerun: python check_identities.py.

notes.summary: A reconstructed conditional on an actual bounded genuine solution with continuous everywhere strictly positive complex Hessian. Actual products, signed admissibility and support annihilation yield singleton supports and every continuous Gateaux derivative; arbitrary continuous F remains untreated.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses local closed Bedford–Taylor factors and radial regularization to identify the actual nonclosed-background bounded products with continuous-form exterior powers. Smooth perturbations of both signs remain genuine and strictly admissible. Their induced continuous logarithmic densities have the same normalization scalar, forcing every actual support to annihilate tr_sigma(dd^c h). The original L^q bounds and n2 identify the supporting probability. Nearby supports converge weakly to it, yielding all directional derivatives. No full real C^2 representative, Dini regularity, rough-current product or Frechet derivative is assumed.
notes.text:
Proof of A. Suppose exactly as stated that the ACTUAL bounded genuine normalized solution u has distributional Hessian sigma=omega+dd^c u represented by a continuous everywhere strictly positive form. No real C^2 representative or modulus of continuity is assumed.

1. Actual bounded-product identification for the nonclosed background.

On a relatively compact holomorphic coordinate ball choose a smooth rho=C|z|^2 with dd^c rho>=omega. Then v=u+rho is genuine locally bounded psh. Put beta=omega-dd^c rho, a smooth form which need not be positive or closed. The local bounded Hermitian product is
(omega+dd^c u)^ell=sum_(j=0)^ell binom(ell,j) beta^(ell-j) wedge (dd^c v)^j. (7)
Each nonsmooth factor is a recursively defined closed Bedford–Taylor product; multiplication by the smooth coefficients of beta is defined on its measure coefficients. No undefined rough-current multiplication occurs.

Take positive radial regularizations v_epsilon decreasing to v on smaller balls. Distributionally dd^c v_epsilon=(dd^c v)*rho_epsilon. Since dd^c v=sigma-omega+dd^c rho has continuous coefficients, these Hessians converge uniformly on compact smaller balls. Thus beta+dd^c v_epsilon converges uniformly to sigma and its algebraic exterior powers converge uniformly to sigma^ell. Expanding those smooth powers as in (7), decreasing Bedford–Taylor continuity identifies their weak limit with the actual bounded product. Therefore the actual product is exactly sigma^ell, for every ell. This also verifies independence of the local choice of rho in this situation: every choice gives the same continuous-form exterior power. The identification is local and hence global and uses no closedness of omega.

2. Genuine signed admissibility and actual linearization.

For real smooth h, compactness and positivity give sigma>=delta tau for a smooth positive tau and delta>0, while dd^c h is bounded relative to tau. Hence sigma_t=sigma+t dd^c h is strictly positive for every sufficiently small |t|, including negative t.

The bounded function u_t=u+t h is a genuine omega-psh representative, not merely an arbitrary a.e. representative. Locally, u_t+rho has positive distributional complex Hessian, so has a unique genuine psh representative. Its radial regularizations tend pointwise to u+t h+rho: the u+rho part has its canonical radial limit and t h converges uniformly. The canonical distribution-to-psh theorem identifies that representative with u_t+rho. The preceding bounded-product argument applies to u_t and identifies its actual product with sigma_t^n.

The original equation is therefore an equality of continuous density forms,
sigma^n=c0(F)exp(F)dV.
Define the continuous real function
F_t=F+log(sigma_t^n/sigma^n).
Every quotient is positive. The actual u_t solves
(omega+dd^c u_t)^n=c0(F)exp(F_t)dV.
Original scalar uniqueness gives B0(F_t)=B0(F).

Ordinary determinant algebra gives, uniformly on X,
F_t=F+t L_sigma h+O_h(t^2), L_sigma h=tr_sigma(dd^c h). (8)
Indeed d/dt log det(S+tD) at zero is tr(S^(-1)D), and S^(-1) is uniformly bounded. Equivalently L_sigma h=n(dd^c h wedge sigma^(n-1))/sigma^n. This is an algebraic product of continuous forms, not multiplication by an unknown maximizing current.

3. Annihilation of EVERY actual supporting probability.

For nu in A0(F), apply its defining inequality to the continuous F_t:
0=B0(F_t)-B0(F)<=-int_X(F_t-F)dnu.
Thus int(F_t-F)dnu<=0 for both signs of t. Divide by t and use (8). The two one-sided limits force
int_X L_sigma h dnu=0 for every real smooth h. (9)
This follows directly from the all-continuous-test supporting inequality and does not assume stationarity.

Fix finite p>2n and p'=p/(p-1). Choose p'<q<n/(n-1). The original L^q bounds give dnu=rho_nu dV with rho_nu in L^(p'). Boundedness of L_sigma, smooth Sobolev density and Holder duality extend (9) to all W^(2,p) tests. By n2, every rho_nu lies in the same one-dimensional annihilator N_p. Their integrals equal1, so all supports coincide. Original nonemptiness yields A0(F)={nu_F}.

4. Gateaux differentiability for every continuous direction.

Monotonicity and the constant-shift rule imply |B0(G)-B0(F)|<=||G-F||_infinity. For real continuous H choose an actual nu_t in A0(F+tH). Every weak accumulation point as t tends to0 lies in A0(F): for arbitrary continuous G pass to the limit in
B0(G)<=B0(F+tH)-int_X(G-F-tH)dnu_t,
using the Lipschitz bound. Probability measures on compact metrizable X have weakly convergent subsequences. Since A0(F) is a singleton, nu_t converges weakly to nu_F regardless of the selections.

For t>0, the support inequalities at F and F+tH give
-int H dnu_t<=[B0(F+tH)-B0(F)]/t<=-int H dnu_F.
For t<0 the corresponding bounds reverse. Weak convergence of nu_t proves that both one-sided quotients tend to -int H dnu_F. Thus
(d/dt)|_(t=0) B0(F+tH)=-int_X H dnu_F
for every real continuous H.

This proves A, using only n1 and the independently reconstructed theorem n2. It asserts Gateaux differentiability, not Frechet differentiability. Uniform Hessian identification uses continuity, and signed admissibility uses the strictly positive lower bound. No existence of such a Hessian for arbitrary continuous original F is provided.

notes.summary: C reconstructed for every compact connected Hermitian k-fold Y: an actual bounded genuine product solution has c0(F)=1 and unique all-test support (A/a)w tensor nu_kappa for every continuous positive A of mean a.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs the sphere potential by smooth zero-mean approximation and the smooth Sobolev inverse. Its pullback has continuous positive Hessian A w+b kappa and actual top product (k+1)A b^k dV. An inverse-block trace identity holds for arbitrary smooth tests. Fubini, sphere Stokes and smooth stationarity identify the proposed probability with an actual support using the one-dimensional annihilator, establishing the inequality for every continuous G. For k=1 the stationary probability is kappa.
notes.text:
Proof of C. Write x for P^1 and y for Y. All forms are pulled back to X=P^1 times Y. Assume int_Y kappa^k=1, int_(P^1)w=1, b=b(x)>0 smooth, A=A(x)>0 continuous, and int Aw=a>0. Set omega=a w+b kappa, dV=w wedge kappa^k, and F=log[(k+1)A b^k]. This retains the original smooth positive background and its nonsingular reference zero; dV is a smooth positive probability.

1. Construct an actual bounded genuine solution.

On the sphere, L_w=tr_w(dd^c) has constants as kernel. Smooth elliptic theory and Stokes give a bounded inverse between zero-mean W^(2,p) and zero-mean L^p for every finite p>1; equivalently use the admitted zero-mean sphere Green kernel. Since int(A-a)w=0, solve
dd^c v=(A-a)w, int v w=0. (10)
For an explicit approximation choose smooth A_j converging uniformly to A and correct their means by replacing A_j with A_j+a-int A_j w. For sufficiently large j they stay positive. Their smooth zero-mean solutions v_j are Cauchy in W^(2,p) by the bounded inverse. Choose p>2(k+1); embedding supplies a bounded real C^(1,alpha) limit v satisfying (10) distributionally. No C^2 or nonsmooth Schauder conclusion is asserted.

Put u(x,y)=v(x). Its distributional Hessian is
sigma=omega+dd^c u=A w+b kappa,
continuous and everywhere strictly positive. Locally add a smooth quadratic with Hessian dominating omega. The resulting continuous function has positive distributional complex Hessian; the canonical psh representative theorem and radial regularization identify it with its genuine psh representative. Thus u is a genuine bounded omega-psh potential.

The actual bounded-product identification of n3 and block exterior algebra give
(omega+dd^c u)^(k+1)=(k+1)A b^k w wedge kappa^k=exp(F)dV.
Hence u actually solves the original equation with scalar1. Original scalar uniqueness gives c0(F)=1 and B0(F)=0.

2. Identify the actual support for EVERY continuous G.

By n3, A0(F) is a singleton and every support annihilates L_sigma. Let nu_kappa be the smooth positive normalized stationary probability of smooth L_kappa, supplied by Gauduchon for k>=2; for k=1 it is kappa by Stokes. Define
mu=(A/a)w tensor nu_kappa.
It is a probability with continuous positive density relative to dV, hence belongs to every finite L^r.

For an arbitrary smooth real phi(x,y), the inverse block matrix gives
L_sigma phi=A^(-1)L_w^x phi+b^(-1)L_kappa^y phi. (11)
The mixed second derivatives make no trace contribution. This formula is not restricted to separated tests. Fubini gives
int_X L_sigma phi dmu
=(1/a)int_Y[int_(P^1)L_w^x phi(x,y)w(x)]dnu_kappa(y)
 +(1/a)int_(P^1)(A(x)/b(x))[int_Y L_kappa^y phi(x,y)dnu_kappa(y)]w(x)=0.
The first inner integral vanishes by Stokes for each fixed y, and the second by stationarity for each fixed x. No coefficient is differentiated.

For p>2(k+1), mu's L^(p') density and smooth Sobolev approximation extend this identity to every W^(2,p) test. The annihilator is one-dimensional by n2. Any actual support exists by the original premise and, by n3, has normalized density in that same line. Therefore it equals mu:
A0(F)={(A/a)w tensor nu_kappa}.
Identifying mu with an actual support proves, for EVERY real continuous G,
B0(G)<=-int_X(G-F)dmu.
Alternatively, concavity and n3's derivative give the same tangent inequality along t to B0(F+t(G-F)). Separated-test stationarity alone is not used as a substitute for this identification.

notes.summary: D reconstructed explicitly on P1 times the dilation Hopf surface: smooth nonclosed omega, strictly positive exp(F), F neither Dini nor Holder of any positive order, c0(F)=1, and unique support (A/a)w tensor kappa^2.
notes.detailedSummary: Fixes the standard moment coordinate tau and verifies its uniform Fubini–Study pushforward. Computes the Hopf rescaling kappa=(4log2)^(-1/2)|z|^(-2)dd^c|z|^2, proves dd^c kappa=0 and stationary probability kappa^2, and gives its uniform logarithmic-radial/angular expression. Verifies genuine nonclosedness and absence of any Kahler metric. Establishes strict positivity of A and exp(F), the actual bounded solution and support through C, and a transverse equatorial lower modulus proving both regularity failures. Symbolic checks supplement the mathematical argument.
notes.text:
Proof of D. Fix the standard smooth moment coordinate
tau([Z0:Z1])=(|Z1|^2-|Z0|^2)/(|Z0|^2+|Z1|^2), -1<=tau<=1.
In z=Z1/Z0 coordinates, w=dd^c log(1+|z|^2) is Fubini–Study probability. Its pushforward by tau is d tau/2: after angular integration w=2r dr/(1+r^2)^2 and d tau=4r dr/(1+r^2)^2.

1. Hopf form, unit volume and stationary probability.

Let Y=(C^2 minus {0})/<z to 2z>, s=|z|^2, Omega=dd^c s and eta=s^(-1)Omega. Dilation multiplies both s and the pulled-back Omega by4, so eta descends to a smooth strictly positive Hermitian form.

With z_j=x_j+i y_j and the required dd^c convention,
Omega=(1/pi)(dx1 wedge dy1+dx2 wedge dy2),
eta^2=(2/pi^2)r^(-4)d lambda_4.
On the fundamental annulus 1<=r<2,
int_Y eta^2=(2/pi^2)|S^3|int_1^2 dr/r=4 log2,
since |S^3|=2pi^2. Therefore
kappa=(4 log2)^(-1/2)eta, int_Y kappa^2=1. (12)

The quotient is smoothly S^3 times S^1, hence connected and compact, and H^2(Y,R)=0. For the two-curve specialization k=1, n4 gives nu_kappa=kappa and nu_F=(A/a)w tensor kappa. Its product-adjoint algebra can be reconstructed explicitly. Set
T=(1/(2a))sigma/b=(1/(2a))[(A/b)w+kappa]. (14)

omega wedge T=(1/(2a))(a+A)w wedge kappa,
so int_X omega wedge T=1 because int Aw=a.

For every smooth phi,
int_X dd^c phi wedge T=(1/(2a))int_X b^(-1)dd^c phi wedge sigma=0.
Indeed sigma^2=2Ab w wedge kappa implies that this integral equals one half of int L_sigma phi dnu_F, which vanishes by n4's full-test calculation.
